title: The highest-fiber nuts

seo.title: Highest-fiber nuts: ranked per 100 g and per serving
seo.meta_description: Almonds and pistachios rank high for fiber, but a real serving is about 1 ounce. Compare fiber per 100 g and per handful.
seo.search_intent: Identify the highest-fiber nuts while translating per-100-g values into realistic portions.

excerpt: Almonds lead many common nuts at about 12.5 g of fiber per 100 g, followed by pistachios and hazelnuts around 10 g. In a 1-ounce serving, that becomes roughly 3–3.5 g of fiber, which is useful but much less dramatic than the 100 g ranking suggests.
content_html:
Nuts are concentrated foods: they pack fiber, fat and calories into a small weight. That makes a per-100-g ranking useful for comparison, but not a great description of how people usually eat them. A typical serving is closer to 1 ounce, or 28 g.

Fiber in common nuts

The table compares plain nuts without coatings or added ingredients.

NutFiber/100 gFiber per 1 oz
Almonds~12.5 g~3.5 g
Pistachios~10.3 g~2.9 g
Hazelnuts~9.7 g~2.7 g
Pecans~9.6 g~2.7 g
Peanuts~8.5 g~2.4 g
Walnuts~6.7 g~1.9 g
Cashews~3.3 g~0.9 g

Almonds do lead, but the gap between almonds and pistachios is well under 1 g of fiber in a normal serving. That is a meaningful difference on paper, not a reason to treat the others as low-fiber foods.

Serving size matters because calories are concentrated too

One hundred grams of almonds provides roughly 579 calories. One ounce is about 164 calories and around 3.5 g of fiber. The serving-level figure is far more useful for planning a snack.

If the goal is simply to increase fiber, it usually makes more sense to combine nuts with legumes, fruit, vegetables and whole grains rather than dramatically increasing nut portions.

Peanuts are the botanical exception

Peanuts are legumes, not tree nuts, but they are eaten like nuts and are useful to include for context. They provide roughly 8.5 g of fiber per 100 g and around 2.4 g per ounce.

Fiber does not arrive alone

An ounce of almonds also provides about 6 g of protein and 14 g of fat, mostly unsaturated. Pistachios and peanuts similarly combine fiber with protein and fat.

That package helps make a modest portion more filling than the same weight of a highly refined snack.

The useful takeaway

Almonds, pistachios, hazelnuts and pecans are among the strongest nut choices for fiber. But the practical difference between the top few is small enough that preference, portion size and overall diet matter more than the exact ranking.

faq.question: Which nut has the most fiber?
faq.answer: Among common nuts, almonds are near the top at about 12.5 g of fiber per 100 g.

faq.question: How much fiber is in an ounce of almonds?
faq.answer: About 3.5 g of fiber per 1-ounce serving.

faq.question: Are cashews high in fiber?
faq.answer: They contain less fiber than almonds or pistachios: about 3.3 g per 100 g, or roughly 0.9 g per ounce.
